chapter: Boots and His Buddies and Wild Cherry
title: Own band in Temple, then joining Walter Wardell and Boots in San Antonio
summary: Steering toward the Wild Cherry record, Harris tells how he led a band in Temple, was recruited by Boots and Walter Wardell for San Antonio, and stayed until the band broke up over money.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: The thing that Paul doesn't know too much about you that I want to give to him. I think the part that he's most interested in is this. Of course all of the background from bringing it up to date is fine. Bringing it up to date is fine. But he recalls hearing the solo that you played with Boots and his buddies on Cherry. Isn't that correct Paul? So I imagine that that is part of the thing that Paul would like to answer.
Perhaps that's most thing he's interested in.
That and I want to ask you to tell me a little later about Lazy Daddy.
I know a question that I play with. Yes that's correct.

I'll play with it. Well then I came out on the house and came on down here and organized a band again in Temple, Texas. I stayed there and while I was there Boots had played with me in Houston and he heard that I was in Temple and Walter Wardell was here organizing the band. Boots told him, I know a way you can get a good first man, a clean tone, nice player. So let's try to get him. Several guys have been trying to get me down here. He brought my hometown, Jack Rampson. He's been trying to get me down here. A lot of guys. But I was doing pretty good in my own little outfit up there in Temple. They didn't have no competition so I stayed there. But I knew sooner or later the town was too small and I wanted to spread out and get bigger I'd have to leave. So when Walter they came up there, talked to me, told my wife, I said, I think I'll take them up. I told her what the deal was. She ran the band for six weeks till I came down here and rehearsed with this guy to try it out. We didn't play a single job for six weeks so I told them, I said, if we don't get some work, I'm going on back to my outfit. So they flew around. Anyway, I stayed with Waddell, they finally got some work, I stayed with Waddell until that band busted up and looked like the same thing happened there that Don C. had trouble with Troy. The money was going one way and I didn't like that going the wrong way.
